_comment: LQR-Fed example configuration.
LQR-Fed replaces binary client removal with continuous per-client aggregation
weights derived by solving a Quadratic Program (QP) each round:
minimise   sum_i [ q * d_i^2 * w_i  +  r * (w_i - 1/N)^2 ]
subject to sum(w) = 1,  0 <= w_i <= 1
where d_i is the L2 distance of client i's weight vector from the reference
centroid. No client is permanently excluded — weights are re-solved every round.
Key hyperparameters:
lqr_q: State cost. Penalty on assigning weight to high-distance clients.
Higher values more aggressively downweight suspicious clients.
Start with q=1.0 and tune upward if attacks are not suppressed.
lqr_r: Control cost. Penalty on deviating from uniform (FedAvg) weights.
Higher values keep the weight distribution closer to equal.
The ratio q/r is the key tuning lever:
q/r >> 1  -> strong outlier suppression
q/r ~  1  -> balanced
q/r << 1  -> near-FedAvg
begin_removing_from_round: Warmup rounds. During warmup the reference
centroid is the arithmetic mean of participant weight vectors.
After warmup the lagged global model is used instead.
Recommended: 5-10 rounds.
